Hi Samantha / Tom —

Quick note ahead of your renewal window in July: we pulled a usage and performance pack for your account covering Mar–May 2026 and wanted to surface a few signals that suggest we should discuss an amendment to your Dedicated commitment. Attached: ACME_usage_Mar-May2026.pdf (high level token spend + per-route breakdown).

Highlights:
- Total token consumption is up ~42% QoQ driven by the customer-facing summarization route (route: /summaries).
- Peak sustained throughput during PST business hours is close to your current Dedicated capacity (we observed 95% utilization for three consecutive weekdays).
- p95 latency for production prompts holding at ~120ms but with occasional spikes to ~320ms during the peak 11:00–13:00 window.

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick 30-min sync this week to review the usage pack and confirm which routes to prioritize for cache/quantization tuning.
2) If you expect similar growth, consider a stepped capacity amendment ( +30% commit with a 10% blended discount ) and an optional 90-day burst buffer.

We can also produce an ROI snapshot (token spend delta vs. expected cost for the proposed commit) if helpful. Monica and Rishi are cc'd for technical and CS context.

Would 11:00–11:30 PT Wed or Thu work for a short review?

Thanks,

— Prioym Das

Hi Samantha —

Attaching the 60-day latency/availability extract and a short cost delta file: latency_report-ACME-2026-05.csv, model_variant_costs.xlsx. Quick summary up front:
- p50/p95/p99 latencies (prod, across /summaries and /chat-assist): 35ms / 120ms / 520ms. The p99 spikes correspond to long-context batch jobs that run around 11:30am.
- Cache hit rate (prefix + KV caching) average: 68% across the last 30 days; /summaries has lower reuse (~42%) because prompts vary more.
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted baseline we used for modeling): $0.032. Under your current Dedicated profile with current utilization, your effective per-1k token unit cost is about $0.028 thanks to sustained utilization.
- Under the +30% commit scenario with a 10% blended discount, the modeled effective per-1k token cost drops to ~$0.024 — ~14% savings vs today, while allowing headroom for growth.

Notes / mitigations:
- If latency spikes are a concern, we can propose: (a) moving /summaries to a variant compiled with attention-optimizations (small perf hit on cost), or (b) reserving a small hot-pool (burst) that absorbs the 11:00–12:00 peak without impacting the main pool.
- If Acme wants to preserve costs, we can selectively quantize non-user-facing routes to reduce token CPU without affecting output quality.

Happy to walk through numbers on Wed.

— Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks Samantha — based on Rishi’s numbers I put together a short amendment draft and a one-page ROI snapshot. Key points in the draft (RDW-Amend-ACME-Dedicated.pdf attached):
- Term: 12 months (rolls automatically), start date: 2026-07-01.
- Commit: +30% GPU capacity (equivalent to 4 additional GPU slots) with a 90-day burst buffer of 2 extra slots.
- Pricing: blended 10% discount vs current effective rate; payment terms remain Net-30 unless procurement requests otherwise.
- SLA addendum: include an explicit p95 latency target of 150ms for production routes; exceptions for scheduled recompiles/maintenance.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan) milestones:
1) This week: review amendment + ROI and finalize preferred capacity number.
2) Next week: procurement to review commercial terms (we can accept DocuSign).
3) 6/15: technical cutover plan (if amendment executes) — Rishi will propose cache/quantization changes before traffic shift.

I pushed the amendment to the HubSpot deal (link below) and shared a Drive folder with the assets. If procurement wants a redline, we can accept edits and iterate quickly.

Wed 11:00 PT still good for me — sending calendar invite.

Best,
— Prioym
